title: Set a short NMR sample's depth: push the tube through the tight spinner to the gauge line (no stop); load the changer
instruction: Put the NMR tube into the spinner in the depth gauge, holding the tube only by its green sleeve, and push it down until its short orange sample is centred on the gauge's black line. Then lift the spinner out by its body and set it in the carousel's open position without moving the tube in it, and let go.
context: Laboratory research automation: every compound made in a synthesis lab is identified by NMR, on shared facility spectrometers, and each user sets their sample's depth by hand. A standard 40-50 mm sample is pushed to the gauge's base, but a shorter one, common when a compound is scarce, must instead be centred on the gauge's line (university NMR facility guides: 'move the tube up in the spinner turbine to keep it centered around the probe center line'), so there is nothing to push against. The 5 mm tube has a 0.4 mm glass wall and the spinner's collar grips it with a few newtons, so it moves in stick-slip and must be stopped within a millimetre by feel and eye. Too low, it breaks in the sample changer or hits the probe's 20 mm lower limit (university NMR facility guides); a fingerprint on the lower part shows in the spectrum. Once set, the spinner is carried by its body ('do NOT move the tube inside the spinner') and lowered into the changer between occupied positions.
setup: Positions from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y to the left arm), heights above the bench top. NMR tube (loose): Wilmad 528-PP-7, borosilicate glass, 5 mm across, 0.43 mm wall, 178 mm long, blue cap, holding 0.40 mL of orange-dyed water (a 30 mm column from 1 mm above its bottom), cap sealed with Parafilm; its top 50 mm in a dark green heat-shrink sleeve; a red paint-marker ring 4 mm wide whose top edge is 80 mm above its bottom; standing in a grey printed rack block (30 x 30 x 40 mm, one 7 mm hole) at (0.22, -0.20). Depth gauge (fixed to the bench): a printed white column 19 mm square on a 70 x 70 x 8 mm grey foot at (0.27, -0.07), a 12 mm bore, the spinner's seat (a 15 mm socket, 16 mm deep, in a round 19 mm collar) at its top, 93 mm up; a clear front window with a mm scale and a black line at 31 mm (62 mm below the seat); a floor stop at 11 mm (20 mm below the line). Spinner (loose): a Bruker-type 5 mm spinner turbine (Wilmad STB-5, white, 24 mm across, 18 mm tall above its shoulder, a 14 mm stem 15 mm long) seated in the gauge. Sample changer carousel segment (fixed): three printed grey seat columns like the gauge's (19 mm square, seat at 93 mm, 32 mm square feet) 55 mm apart in a row at (0.276, 0.110), (0.30, 0.16) and (0.324, 0.210); the outer two each hold a spinner with a tube set to depth (same parts); the middle one is open, with the same window, scale and line and no floor near the tube's end (its bore runs to 6 mm).
scoring: Measured at the end, everything still for 1 s. 0 if at any time: the tube is dropped (tips past 30 degrees or its bottom reaches the bench outside the rack, gauge or carousel position) or the spinner falls; a gripper touches the tube below the red band, or any other part of the robot touches the tube (trial video); the spinner is lifted off a seat with no gripper on its body (carried by the tube); either neighbouring spinner is lifted, tipped or shifted off its seat (video; in simulation, 2 mm or 2 degrees). Otherwise 0 unless the tube is through the spinner, upright within 3 degrees, the spinner seated (shoulder on the seat, centred) in the gauge or in the carousel's open position, and both grippers 4 cm clear of tube and spinner. Then, by how far the column's centre is from the line, read on the gauge's or the open position's mm scale (photo, front): 0.25 if more than 3 mm; 0.5 within 3 mm; 0.75 within 1 mm in the gauge; 1.0 within 1 mm in the carousel. Pushing the tube to the gauge's floor leaves the column 4 mm low: 0.25.
reset_notes: Lift the spinner out of the changer by its body, slide the tube out of it, wipe the tube's lower part with a lint-free tissue, stand it back in the rack and seat the spinner in the gauge. A chipped or cracked tube is replaced (same part); if a tube breaks, stop the trial and clear the shards before the next one.
fidelity: PhysX at 240 Hz. The spinner's grip on the tube is two rings of four sprung rollers in its bore (500 N/m, 0.6 N preload each), about 3 N of sliding friction: an estimate of a real spinner's 'comfortable resistance'; the robot pushes the tube against it. Glass is rigid and cannot break; the tube weighs 20 g in simulation (real about 6 g) for steady contacts. Changer positions are 55 mm apart, wider than a real carousel's, for the YAM's fingers. The liquid is drawn, not simulated.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right arm, on the right of the video, rose over the tube rack and hovered 6-7 cm from the tube without gripping it; the left arm reached toward the carousel at 30 s, then drew back; nothing was touched). Scripted demo: 1.0 (column 0.2 mm off the line, in the carousel).
